subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should this be fixed by changing the scheduled memory/heartbeat producer, by changing generic read-tool directory semantics, or by first requiring live gateway memory-growth reproduction?
rationale: Current source proves partial slices but not the remaining producer or RSS-growth mechanism, and the directory-as-file expectation would change a model-facing tool contract.

options.title: Require Live Scheduler Proof First
options.body: Keep this issue open until a current-main gateway run captures the repeated producer, file-read failures, and RSS trend together.

options.title: Fix Producer-Only Behavior
options.body: Treat the read errors as bad scheduled prompts or memory guidance and update that producer once identified, without changing the generic read tool contract.

options.title: Change Read Tool Semantics
options.body: Make read list or redirect directories, accepting a broader model-facing behavior change that needs maintainer-owned compatibility judgment.

recommendation.title: Require Live Scheduler Proof First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a current-main gateway run captures the repeated producer, file-read failures, and RSS trend together.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main read/gateway maintenance makes this the best available owner for the unresolved tool-contract versus producer decision.
